text: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius at sea level, but at higher altitudes the lower air pressure makes it boil at a lower temperature.
The Nile flows north through Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean Sea, and its annual floods once made the surrounding soil unusually fertile.
A leap year has 366 days instead of 365, with the extra day added to February so that the calendar stays aligned with Earth's orbit around the Sun.
Photosynthesis allows green plants to turn sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen, which is why forests are often called the lungs of the planet.
The printing press, introduced in Europe in the fifteenth century, made books cheaper and helped ideas spread much faster than copying by hand ever could.
In a right triangle the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides, a rule known as the Pythagorean theorem.
Bread dough rises because yeast feeds on sugars and releases carbon dioxide, which becomes trapped in the stretchy network formed by gluten.
The Moon completes one orbit around Earth roughly every twenty-seven days, and it always shows the same face to us because its rotation matches its orbit.
A noun names a person, place, thing or idea, while a verb describes an action or a state of being; most sentences need at least one of each.
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they shelter about a quarter of all known marine species.
The Great Wall of China was built and rebuilt over many centuries by different dynasties, mainly to protect against raids from the north.
Electric current is the flow of charged particles, usually electrons in a wire, and it is measured in amperes.
Many desert plants store water in thick stems or leaves and have waxy surfaces that slow evaporation under the strong sun.
The Amazon rainforest holds the largest river basin in the world and is home to an enormous variety of insects, birds, fish and mammals.
Compound interest means that interest is earned on both the original amount and on interest already added, so savings grow faster over long periods.
A symphony orchestra is usually divided into four sections: strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion, each contributing a different colour of sound.
Glaciers are slow rivers of ice that form where more snow falls in winter than melts in summer, and they carve valleys as they move.
The human heart beats about one hundred thousand times a day, pushing blood through a network of vessels that would stretch many thousands of kilometres.
Mount Everest, on the border between Nepal and China, is the highest mountain above sea level, rising to nearly nine thousand metres.
A haiku is a short Japanese poem traditionally made of three lines with five, seven and five syllables, often describing a moment in nature.
Rainbows appear when sunlight is refracted and reflected inside water droplets, splitting the light into its component colours.
The Roman Empire built roads, aqueducts and public baths across Europe, and many of these structures are still standing today.
In chess each player starts with sixteen pieces, and the game ends when one king is trapped so that it cannot escape capture.
Honey bees communicate the location of flowers to each other through a pattern of movements known as the waggle dance.
Sound travels as a wave of pressure through air, water or solid material, and it moves faster in water than in air.
The metric system is based on powers of ten, which makes converting between units such as metres, centimetres and kilometres simple.
Volcanoes form where molten rock from deep inside the Earth finds a path to the surface, building cones of ash and hardened lava over time.
A balanced breakfast might include whole grains, fruit and a source of protein, which together provide steady energy through the morning.
Libraries lend books, host reading groups and often offer quiet rooms and free internet access for the whole community.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth, covering more area than all of the land combined.
Recycling aluminium cans saves most of the energy needed to make new aluminium from raw ore, which is why collection programs exist in many cities.
Penguins live almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere, and their dense feathers and layer of fat keep them warm in freezing water.
A bridge can be supported in different ways, such as beams, arches, cables or trusses, depending on the distance it has to span and the loads it must carry.
The periodic table arranges the chemical elements by atomic number, and elements in the same column tend to behave in similar ways.
Marathons are run over forty-two kilometres, a distance that commemorates a legendary run from a battlefield to the city of Athens.
Tides are caused mainly by the gravity of the Moon pulling on the oceans, producing two high tides and two low tides in most places each day.
The first step in writing a clear essay is to decide on a single main point, then arrange the supporting ideas in a sensible order.
Silk is made from the cocoon of the silkworm, and for centuries the method of producing it was a closely guarded secret in China.
A thermometer measures temperature, while a barometer measures air pressure, and meteorologists use both to forecast the weather.
Olive trees can live for hundreds of years, and their fruit is pressed to make oil that is central to cooking around the Mediterranean.
Planets in our solar system travel around the Sun in elliptical paths, and the planets closest to the Sun complete their orbits much faster.
Learning to read music involves recognising notes on a staff, understanding rhythm, and following signs that tell the player how loudly or softly to play.
Many languages share common roots; for example, Spanish, French, Italian and Portuguese all descend from the Latin spoken in the Roman Empire.
Wind turbines convert the motion of moving air into electricity, and they are often placed on hills or offshore where the wind is steady.
The skeleton of an adult human has two hundred and six bones, which protect organs, support the body and anchor the muscles.
A recipe for pancakes usually combines flour, eggs, milk and a little salt into a smooth batter that is poured onto a hot, lightly oiled pan.
Satellites orbiting the Earth help with navigation, weather forecasting and communication by relaying signals across great distances.
The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the eighteenth century and changed how goods were made by introducing machines and factories.
In geometry a circle is the set of all points at the same distance from a centre, and the distance around it is called the circumference.
Tea is made by steeping the dried leaves of a plant in hot water, and different drying methods produce green, black or oolong varieties.
Earthquakes occur when stress built up along a crack in the Earth's crust is suddenly released, sending waves of energy through the ground.
A budget is a plan for how to spend money over a period of time, usually by listing expected income and then assigning amounts to each expense.
The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, spanning much of northern Africa, with vast stretches of sand dunes and rocky plateaus.
Public transport such as buses, trams and trains moves many people at once, which can reduce traffic and lower pollution in busy cities.
Cheese is made by curdling milk, draining the liquid whey, and then pressing and aging the remaining curds for days, months or even years.
A prime number is a whole number greater than one that can only be divided evenly by one and itself, such as two, three, five and seven.
The Renaissance was a period of renewed interest in art, science and learning that began in Italy and spread across Europe from the fourteenth century.
Bats are the only mammals capable of true flight, and many species find their way and their food in the dark by listening to echoes.
Good posture while sitting at a desk means keeping the feet flat, the back supported and the screen at a comfortable height for the eyes.
Rivers carry sediment downstream and deposit it where the current slows, gradually building up flat areas of land called deltas.
A camera lens focuses light onto a sensor or film, and a wider opening lets in more light but also makes the area in focus shallower.
Glass is made by heating sand with other minerals until it melts, and it can be shaped while hot and then left to cool into a hard, clear solid.
The seasons are caused by the tilt of Earth's axis, which changes how directly sunlight reaches each part of the planet during the year.
A good map includes a scale, a legend explaining its symbols, and a compass direction so that readers can understand distances and orientation.
Elephants are the largest land animals, living in family groups led by an older female, and they use low rumbling sounds to keep in touch.
Paper is traditionally made from wood pulp that is mixed with water, spread into thin sheets, pressed and dried.
Basic first aid for a small cut includes washing the wound with clean water, applying gentle pressure to stop the bleeding and covering it with a bandage.
The Olympic Games began in ancient Greece and were revived in the late nineteenth century, now bringing athletes from nearly every country together.
In a spreadsheet, each cell can hold a number, a piece of text or a formula that calculates a value from other cells.
A lighthouse uses a powerful lamp and a system of lenses to send a beam of light far across the water, warning ships of nearby rocks.
Soil is a mixture of tiny rock particles, decaying plant matter, water and air, and earthworms help keep it loose and rich in nutrients.
The telephone was patented in the late nineteenth century, and over the following decades networks of wires connected homes and businesses.
Mathematics uses symbols to express relationships precisely; for example, an equation states that two expressions have the same value.
Lakes form in hollows left by glaciers, in basins created by moving land, or behind natural dams, and they can hold fresh or salty water.
A sailboat moves by using the wind that fills its sails, and a skilled sailor can travel across the wind or even partly against it by changing angles.
Fermentation is a process in which microorganisms break down sugars, and it is used to make foods such as yogurt, pickles, sourdough bread and many drinks.
The alphabet used in English has twenty-six letters, though the number of distinct sounds in spoken English is considerably larger.
A museum collects and preserves objects of historical, artistic or scientific interest and displays them so that visitors can learn from them.
Magnets have two poles, and opposite poles attract while matching poles push apart, a behaviour that is used in compasses and electric motors.
Whales are mammals that breathe air through blowholes, and many species travel thousands of kilometres each year between feeding and breeding areas.
To change a flat bicycle tyre, remove the wheel, take out the punctured inner tube, fit a new one, and pump it up to the pressure printed on the tyre.
The Mississippi River flows south through the middle of the United States and has been a major route for transporting goods for centuries.
Clouds are made of tiny water droplets or ice crystals, and they form when warm moist air rises, cools and the water vapour condenses.
An index at the back of a book lists topics in alphabetical order together with the pages where they are discussed.
The cello is a large string instrument played while seated, with the player holding it between the knees and drawing a bow across the strings.
Bricks are made by shaping clay into blocks and firing them in a kiln, and builders have used them for thousands of years because they are durable.
Time zones divide the world into regions that share the same standard time, so that noon is roughly when the Sun is highest in the sky.
A simple machine such as a lever or a pulley lets a person lift a heavy object with less effort by spreading the force over a longer distance.
Spices such as cinnamon, pepper and cloves were once so valuable that they shaped trade routes and led explorers to sail to distant lands.
The Arctic is a frozen ocean surrounded by land, while Antarctica is a frozen continent surrounded by ocean, and both are extremely cold.
An orchestra conductor keeps the musicians together by setting the tempo and giving cues, using movements of the hands and a baton.
A forest ecosystem includes trees, shrubs, fungi, insects and animals, all of which depend on one another for food, shelter and nutrients.
Calendars have been built around the cycles of the Moon, the Sun or both, and different cultures still mark New Year on different dates.
A pendulum swings back and forth at a steady rate that depends mainly on its length, which is why it was used to regulate early clocks.
Traffic lights use red, yellow and green signals in a fixed order to let vehicles and pedestrians take turns crossing a junction safely.
The Danube is the second longest river in Europe and flows through or alongside ten countries before reaching the Black Sea.
Stretching gently before and after exercise can help muscles stay flexible and may reduce stiffness in the following day.
A telescope gathers more light than the human eye, which allows astronomers to see faint stars and distant galaxies.
Maple trees turn bright red and orange in autumn as the green pigment fades and other pigments in the leaves become visible.
A dictionary lists words in alphabetical order, giving their spellings, pronunciations and meanings, and often examples of how they are used.
Potatoes originated in the Andes mountains of South America and were carried to Europe in the sixteenth century, where they became a staple food.
Ice floats on water because water expands as it freezes, making ice slightly less dense than the liquid around it.
Solar panels contain cells that convert sunlight directly into electricity, and they work best when pointed toward the Sun without shade.

messages.content: How do I boil an egg?
Place the egg in a pot of water, bring it to a boil, then turn off the heat and let it sit covered for about ten minutes for a hard-boiled egg. Cool it in cold water before peeling.
What is the capital of France?
The capital of France is Paris.
Can you explain what a noun is?
A noun is a word that names a person, place, thing or idea, such as teacher, river, table or freedom.
Why is the sky blue?
Air scatters short blue wavelengths of sunlight more strongly than longer red ones, so blue light reaches our eyes from every direction of the sky.
What is ten percent of two hundred?
Ten percent of two hundred is twenty.
Give me a tip for studying.
Study in short focused sessions with small breaks, and test yourself on the material instead of only rereading it.
How many days are there in a week?
There are seven days in a week.
What does a thermometer measure?
A thermometer measures temperature.
How do plants make food?
Plants make food through photosynthesis, using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to produce sugar and oxygen.
Name three primary colours.
Red, yellow and blue are the traditional primary colours in painting, while red, green and blue are the primary colours of light.
What is the opposite of hot?
The opposite of hot is cold.
How can I make tea?
Heat fresh water until it is nearly boiling, pour it over a tea bag or loose leaves, let it steep for three to five minutes, then remove the leaves and enjoy.
What is a synonym for happy?
Some synonyms for happy are cheerful, glad, joyful and content.
Why do we have seasons?
We have seasons because Earth's axis is tilted, so different parts of the planet receive more direct sunlight at different times of the year.
Can you tell me a fun fact about octopuses?
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood, and they can squeeze through any opening larger than their beak.
How do I convert kilometres to metres?
Multiply the number of kilometres by one thousand, since one kilometre equals one thousand metres.
What is the largest planet in the solar system?
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
How do I write a polite email?
Start with a greeting, state your purpose clearly in the first sentence, keep the message short, and close with a courteous sign-off and your name.
What is the boiling point of water?
Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius, or two hundred and twelve degrees Fahrenheit, at sea level.
Who painted the Mona Lisa?
The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci in the early sixteenth century.
What is an adjective?
An adjective is a word that describes a noun, such as tall, red or delicious.
How many sides does a hexagon have?
A hexagon has six sides.
Suggest a healthy snack.
An apple with a spoonful of peanut butter, a handful of nuts or some carrot sticks with hummus are all healthy snacks.
What does a library do?
A library lends books and other materials, offers quiet places to read and study, and often provides free access to computers and the internet.
How do airplanes stay in the air?
Their wings are shaped so that moving air produces lift, and the engines provide the forward speed needed to keep that airflow going.
What is the square root of sixty-four?
The square root of sixty-four is eight.
Explain what a river delta is.
A delta is a landform where a river slows and splits into smaller channels as it enters a larger body of water, depositing sediment that builds up new land.
How do I keep a houseplant healthy?
Give it light suited to its type, water it only when the top of the soil feels dry, and make sure the pot has drainage holes.
What language is spoken in Brazil?
Portuguese is the main language spoken in Brazil.
Give me an example of a metaphor.
Saying that time is a thief is a metaphor, because it describes time as something that steals moments without using the word like or as.
What is the freezing point of water?
Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius, or thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit.
How do magnets work?
Magnets produce a magnetic field that attracts certain metals such as iron, and opposite poles pull toward each other while matching poles push apart.
What is a good way to start a speech?
Begin with a short story, a surprising fact or a question that draws the audience in, and then state what you will talk about.
How many continents are there?
There are seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America and South America.
What does recycling mean?
Recycling means collecting used materials such as paper, glass, metal and plastic and processing them so they can be made into new products.
What is the difference between weather and climate?
Weather describes conditions in a place over a short time, such as today's rain, while climate is the typical pattern of weather over many years.
How can I improve my handwriting?
Slow down, practise forming each letter carefully, and use lined paper so that your letters stay a consistent size.
Tell me about the Moon.
The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite. It orbits our planet about every twenty-seven days and its gravity is the main cause of the ocean tides.
What is a healthy amount of sleep for adults?
Most adults do well with seven to nine hours of sleep each night.
How does a refrigerator keep food cold?
It circulates a fluid that absorbs heat from the inside and releases it outside, so the interior stays cool.
Spell the word necessary.
The word is spelled n-e-c-e-s-s-a-r-y.
What is a mammal?
A mammal is a warm-blooded animal that has hair or fur and feeds its young with milk, such as dogs, whales and humans.
Can you suggest a name for a lighthouse in a story?
How about Harbour Light, Silverrock Beacon or the Last Lantern?
What is photosynthesis in one sentence?
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants use sunlight to turn water and carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen.
How do I find the area of a rectangle?
Multiply its length by its width.
What causes thunder?
Thunder is the sound made when lightning heats the air so quickly that it expands explosively and sends out a shock wave.
Recommend a way to relax after a long day.
You could take a short walk, listen to calm music, or spend a few minutes breathing slowly and stretching.
What is the longest river in the world?
The Nile and the Amazon are the two longest rivers, and which is longer depends on how the length is measured.
How do I tie a simple knot?
Cross one end of the rope over the other, tuck it under and through the loop, and pull both ends firmly to tighten it.
What is an ecosystem?
An ecosystem is a community of living things interacting with each other and with their physical environment, such as a pond or a forest.
How many minutes are in an hour?
There are sixty minutes in an hour.
